notes.summary: Compact boundary, full-support lifts and exact conductor/completion rules pass for excellent positive-dimensional local reduction; nilpotents and empty field factors are handled.
notes.detailedSummary: Reconstructs bounded positive primary-gauge denominators, quotient-first finite field lifts, normalization local centres, finite OPEN singleton fibres and CLOSED quotient fibres at infinity. Completion covers all supports and primary contraction is exact.
notes.text:
Independent review of ACTUAL FINAL n1: mathematics PASS; essential sources PASS.

Throughout, R is an excellent Noetherian local ring, replaced by its reduction, and a is a proper m-primary ideal. The normalized boundary consists of all real semivaluations v with v(a)=1; supports may be nonminimal primes. Nilpotents have value infinity. A zero-dimensional local reduction is a field and has empty boundary. All later statements about nonempty sections concern positive dimension.

Here is the topological construction without a supplied correctness grant. In [0,infinity]^R, the semivaluation identities, v(1)=0, and v(m)=1 are closed conditions: extended addition and minimum are continuous, and the inequality for sums is closed. Finite generation makes v(m) a finite minimum. Thus this section is compact Hausdorff. Choose r,s>0 with m^r contained in a contained in m^s. Then s v(m)<=v(a)<=r v(m). Division by v(a) identifies the m-section with the a-section. For two primary gauges a,b, the ray-preserving map is v -> v/v(b), and a homogeneous function transforms by u_b(v/v(b))=u_a(v)/v(b). The denominator is continuous, positive and bounded above and below on the compact section, so the transformations and their inverses preserve uniform closure and decreasing nets. Composition gives the exact cocycle. Nonprimary gauges lack these bounds and only define partial sections.

Nonemptiness follows by taking a one-dimensional domain quotient of R, normalizing it (finite by excellence), and taking a DVR at a closed normalization centre. Pulling its order back gives an allowed semivaluation. Minimal primes alone do not index boundary branches or normalization centres.

For a finite injection R -> B with B reduced, every boundary point lifts to the FULL boundary of B, the finite disjoint union of local-centre boundaries normalized by aB. First quotient R by the given support p, choose P in B above p, and work with the finite field extension Frac(R/p) -> Frac(B/P). Extend the valuation there, rather than extending a supportful semivaluation to Frac(R). A valuation-ring extension exists by integral closure, lying over and a maximal dominating local overring. The elementary maximal-overring argument is this: if both x and x^{-1} failed membership, adjoining them and then localizing at a prime above the old maximal ideal would contradict maximality; if that maximal ideal generated the unit ideal after adjoining x^{-1}, the resulting equation makes x integral, and its adjunction still has a prime above it. Thus the maximal overring is a valuation ring. Its intersection with the old field is the old valuation ring. Algebraicity makes each new value an integral rational multiple of an old value, by comparing least terms in an algebraic equation; its ordered group therefore embeds in the divisible hull of the original real group. Integrality makes values nonnegative on B/P. The lift is centered at a closed local centre because aB has the same closed-point support over m. This proves surjectivity including nonminimal supports. Every full fibre is retained; extra vertical components are allowed. A zero-dimensional source factor has aB=0, hence no normalized boundary point. It contributes no spurious valuation or degree. Compact surjectivity gives a quotient map.

Let S be the finite normalization. Clearing denominators of finitely many S-generators gives a regular element in the conductor c=Ann_R(S/R), and R=S x_{S/c} R/c as rings: an element of S whose residue lies in R/c already lies in R. Normalization boundary pieces are indexed by maximal local CENTRES of S above m, not just its minimal primes. Finite generation and Chinese remainders separate these pieces by clopen subsets. If v(c)<infinity, pick c in the conductor with finite value. Any lift must satisfy w(s)=v(cs)-v(c), so the fibre is a singleton. At v(c)=infinity, precisely the boundary fibres of (S/c)_red -> (R/c)_red are identified. This stratum is CLOSED; the finite-conductor stratum is OPEN. Quotient topology descends fibre-constant continuous and upper semicontinuous functions, but says nothing by itself about positivity.

Completion also retains ALL supports. If F in Rhat is represented by f_N modulo m^N, the values v(f_N) stabilize whenever they lie below N v(m); otherwise the limiting value is infinity. This defines vhat(F). The same truncation argument proves addition, multiplication and the valuation inequality, uniqueness and continuity. With a-normalization, v(m)>=1/r; applying t -> t/(1+t), truncation changes a value by at most 1/(1+N/r), uniformly over the section. Restriction and extension are inverse homeomorphisms. If a completed primary ideal J contains mhat^N, its image in Rhat/mhat^N=R/m^N has finitely many lifts in R. These lifts together with m^N generate J, proving J=(J intersect R)Rhat and proper-primary contraction. No completion theorem for arbitrary nonnormal irreducibility is being asserted.

This reconstructs the actual n1 claims. Ordinary Noetherian finite-generation, excellence/Nagata normalization and valuation-ring background are used at their stated hypotheses; no historical helper or ROOT reading metadata is a premise. The full review is retained in whole-proof.md; exact inputs are in exact-input-hashes.json. Rerun the read-only integrity check with python review_audit.py.

notes.summary: All-component integral dependence and one common contraction exponent pass; normal-domain Izumi and excellent-domain residue hypotheses are checked.
notes.detailedSummary: Zero-dimensional nonunit components require Q-image zero, supplied by a positive boundary-ideal power. Finite graded-algebra generation gives the common exponent. Exact normal completion, dimension formula and Rees residue degree justify the characteristic-free nonunit order bound; units are separate.
notes.text:
Independent review of ACTUAL FINAL n2: mathematics PASS; essential sources PASS.

Use the boundary and full-support lifting proved in LOCAL n1. The integral-dependence statement needed later concerns a Noetherian semilocal algebra E, an ideal J containing a power of the boundary ideal aE, and Q with w(Q)>=w(J) on every centered normalized semivaluation. Every minimal component is tested. On a positive-dimensional domain component where J is proper, the centered rank-one DVR criterion of Swanson--Huneke 6.8.3--4 shows Q is integral over J. All such DVRs are allowed boundary points because aE is primary at that centre. Unit components impose no condition. On a zero-dimensional component where J has zero image, the boundary is empty and valuation testing alone proves nothing: the additional hypothesis Q-image=0 is necessary. Our later Q=K(aE)^L with L>0 satisfies exactly this hypothesis, since aE vanishes on that component.

This componentwise conclusion lifts to E. For x in Q choose a monic equation modulo each minimal prime with coefficients in the corresponding J-powers, lift its coefficients, and multiply the equations. The product is in the nilradical; raising it to a nilpotence exponent gives a monic equation for x with coefficients in J^i. This is the immediate argument in book 1.1.5, and it covers nonreduced conductor quotients. Importantly, the exponent needed in contraction is not chosen pointwise from the valuation inequalities. The graded algebra E[(J+Q)t] is finite over E[Jt]: each Qt-generator is integral, and both sets of generators are finite. Choose homogeneous module generators of degrees at most h. In degree N+h each term contains at least N factors from J. Consequently Q^{N+h} is contained in (J+Q)^{N+h}, which is contained in J^N, for every N>=1. This proves one common h. Book 1.2.3--5 gives the equivalent reduction argument; its integral-closure bars were checked in the primary PDF, printed page 6.

The density argument in n6 will also need a divisorial order bound. Rees valuations exist for a nonzero proper primary ideal of an excellent local domain by the full proof of book 10.2.2, including its 10.2.3 continuation: normalized Rees charts are Krull rings with finitely many relevant height-one primes, and the fixed-denominator argument brings their inequalities back to the original ring. At a formally equidimensional local target, 10.4.3 gives residue transcendence degree dim(A)-1. Excellence implies universal catenarity; B.5.1 gives the needed formal equidimensionality. For a finite-type birational domain chart B0 and P above the closed point, B.3.2 gives dim(B0_P)+trdeg_k kappa(P)=dim(A). Its immediate proof is B.2.5 with equality: in the algebraic one-generator step S=A[X]/I, catenarity of A[X] changes ht(Q)+ht(I)<=ht(Q') into equality; the transcendental step is already an equality, and induction over generators and transcendence-degree additivity completes the formula. Thus the claimed modification is accounted for.

For an excellent NORMAL local domain A, exact Stacks 0C23, Lemma 15.53.6, implies Ahat is normal because its formal fibres are normal. The complete local normal ring is a domain, so A is analytically irreducible and analytically unramified. This is not a statement about arbitrary nonnormal completions. Rond--Spivakovsky v1 Theorem 1.3 applies to this analytically irreducible DOMAIN. Compare a fixed divisorial nu with each of the finitely many m-Rees valuations nu_j, obtaining nu(f)<=C0 min_j nu_j(f)/nu_j(m)=C0 barord_m(f). Theorem 1.4 gives barord_m(f)<=ord_m(f)+K. For a nonzero nonunit, ord_m(f)>=1, hence nu(f)<=C0(1+K)ord_m(f). Units have both sides zero and are handled separately; zero has infinite value. The literal strict inequality in their Remark 1.6 must not be applied to units. Swanson's entire Section 5 was checked, but its complete-domain theorem is not used as a theorem for an arbitrary domain.

The precise sources just listed were read with their immediate proofs and contexts, not imported as candidate notes. Printed book page 140 confirms the bars in 6.8.3--4. Historical Rees, Izumi, Ratliff and formal-fibre foundations are ordinary published dependencies, not claims of recursively fresh proofs. Source applications and qualifications are recorded in whole-source-application-ledger.md; rerun selected pixel extraction with python inspect_bound_pages.py.

notes.summary: The rational difference lattice and canonical normal-domain trace pass with full fibres, inseparable lengths and primary-gauged continuity.
notes.detailedSummary: Uniform closure gives a REAL lattice without an irrational integer formula. Norm coefficients lie in the normal target; quotient Gauss valuations cover nonminimal supports. Finite fibre measures have full support and normalized positive weights at least 1/n; arbitrary vertical sources receive no invented generic degree.
notes.text:
Independent review of ACTUAL FINAL n3: mathematics PASS; essential sources PASS.

Use LOCAL n1. Write Q_R for finite nonnegative REAL sums of -v(I), with I proper primary or the unit ideal; C_R is their uniform closure among finite continuous functions; D_R consists of pointwise infima of NONEMPTY decreasing C_R-NETS. It includes zero and bottom. On a finite semilocal boundary the construction is the product of its local-centre constructions: modulo a sufficiently large common primary power, Chinese remainders glue ideals proper at selected centres and unit at others. Empty zero-dimensional factors impose no boundary conditions. Rational coefficient approximation and ideal products show that single profiles -v(I)/k are uniformly dense in C_R. C_R is a convex cone stable under maxima, since max(-v(I),-v(J))=-v(I+J); real coefficients follow by uniform approximation. Sums and maxima of D-elements use the product of their directed index sets. They do not require flattening arbitrary nested nets or closure under increasing limits or subtraction.

For later trace continuity the rational DIFFERENCE span of ideal-value functions is a lattice. After common denominators, min(v(I)-v(J),v(K)-v(H))=v(IH+KJ)-v(JH). Constants come from v(a)=1. These functions separate points: a differing coordinate v(f) can be truncated by replacing (f) with (f)+a^N, choosing N above a differing finite threshold. Its UNIFORM closure is a REAL vector lattice, not an integer ideal formula for irrational coefficients. To see density in all real continuous functions on the compact boundary, separation and constants allow two-point affine interpolation. Finite minima patch upper estimates around one point; finite maxima patch lower estimates over the compact space. The usual lattice approximation then gives arbitrary uniform accuracy. This proof also states where passage from rational to real coefficients occurs.

Now let A be an excellent normal local DOMAIN and B a finite domain A-algebra of field degree n. In a finite normal extension M containing all embeddings of L=Frac(B), let Sigma be those embeddings and q the inseparable degree; n=q|Sigma|. For finite generators b_i of a boundary-primary J, the generic norm polynomial is product over sigma of (sum T_i sigma(b_i))^q. This formula follows by splitting the finite algebra over an algebraic closure: each embedding has the same purely inseparable generic length q. Its coefficients lie in K=Frac(A) and are integral over A; normality puts them in A. Let N(J) be their coefficient ideal. Changing generators substitutes linear forms and gives both ideal inclusions, so N(J) is intrinsic. For x in a sufficiently large primary power contained in J, the pure coefficient x^n belongs to N(J); hence its radical contains m. Its properness when required follows from the valuation formula below. No flatness is assumed.

Normalize A in M, obtaining finite E. Lift ANY supportful v of A to E by the quotient-first procedure in n1. Compose with each embedding to get w_sigma on B. On the support quotient, the Gauss value of a polynomial is the minimum of its coefficient values; it is multiplicative because the leading residue polynomials are nonzero and their product is nonzero. Applying this to the norm polynomial proves v(N(J))=q sum_sigma w_sigma(J) for ALL supports, not just fraction-field valuations of A. Thus mu_v=q sum_sigma delta_{w_sigma} has mass n. Its moments on ideal profiles are intrinsic by the formula, and on their dense real lattice by the preceding approximation; this proves independence of the chosen lift, hence defines a canonical measure. Every point of the FULL fibre over v extends from B to E (E is finite integral over the chosen copy of B), and appears as one of these w_sigma after taking that extension. Therefore every fibre point has mass at least 1, and after division by n at least 1/n. No defectless e*f formula was used; inseparability is included by q.

For continuous H, define TH(v)=integral H dmu_v. The coefficient formula makes T continuous on the primary-gauged lattice; density and ||T||<=n give continuity for every H. On -w(J)/k, T returns -v(N(J))/k; thus T(C_B) is contained in C_A by approximation. For a fibre-constant u=h composed with restriction, T(u)=nh. The full finite fibre and its positive masses also let decreasing limits commute with this sum, including bottom values. If u is given by a decreasing C_B-net, its normalized traces form an ACTUAL decreasing C_A-net with limit h. This proves both continuous and D-descent over a normal domain target.

For a reduced finite source with vertical components, take traces ONLY on its generic-dominating domain components and divide by the sum of those genuine generic degrees. Their boundaries still cover the target (lying over holds on each dominating finite domain); a function constant on the actual full fibres has the same value on these lifts and on vertical lifts. Thus the descent conclusion applies without assigning an invented generic degree to a vertical component. This does not claim an unrestricted canonical degree trace for arbitrary reduced finite sources. General reduced-target descent will use normalization and reduced base change in n4--n6, not this formula with hypotheses removed.

This reconstructs actual n3, with the full-fibre and primary-gauge continuity qualifications retained. The relevant algebra and valuation facts were proved here or in n1; no e*f, supplied checker or ROOT metadata is a mathematical premise. The artifact whole-proof.md contains the complete local support chain.

notes.summary: Continuous positive descent passes by exact conductor contraction and compact approximation, including arbitrary reduced finite injections.
notes.detailedSummary: Uses dimension induction, ALL components, a common integral-dependence exponent and internal dyadic monotonicity. Finite-conductor errors and quotient estimates at infinity are separated. Reduced base change is injective by spectra. Only Q subset N subset C and equal uniform closures are claimed.
notes.text:
Independent review of ACTUAL FINAL n4: mathematics PASS; essential sources PASS.

Use LOCAL n1--n3. I reconstruct continuous positive descent by induction on the dimension of the reduced local target. Dimension zero has empty boundary. Normal local domain targets are settled by n3; semilocal normal targets are treated centre by centre. For the remaining normalization step R subset S, let c be its conductor, C0=R/c and E=S/c. The conductor contains a regular element, so dim(C0_red)<dim R. Let u in C_S be constant on every actual normalization fibre, and h its continuous quotient function. Its restriction to the closed infinite-conductor stratum is h0 in C_(C0_red), by the induction hypothesis applied to C0_red subset E_red. Restriction of primary ideal profiles to a positive-dimensional quotient is primary; a zero-dimensional quotient contributes no boundary point.

Fix epsilon>0. Choose j=-w(J)/k approximating u and kappa=-v(K)/k approximating h0 within epsilon, with common denominator and 1/k<epsilon. On positive-dimensional centres J can be made proper by a tiny negative primary correction. A zero-dimensional factor may be assigned a zero or unit ideal according to its quotient component; it is not an extra boundary condition. On E, the valuation difference between KE and JE is bounded by 2k epsilon. Choose a positive integer L with 2k epsilon<L<=2k epsilon+1. Then Q=KE(aE)^L has w(Q)>=w(JE) on every normalized point. The positive power ensures Q has zero image on every zero-dimensional minimal component where JE is nonunit. LOCAL n2 proves integral dependence on ALL components and supplies ONE exponent h' with Q^{N+h'} contained in (JE)^N for every N.

Set I_N=J^N intersect R. These are actual proper primary ideals: J contains a power of aS, hence I_N contains a power of a; properness follows at a positive-dimensional dominating centre. Contraction modulo the conductor is EXACT:
  (I_N+c)/c=(JE)^N intersect C0.
Indeed if a residue of x in J^N lies in R/c, then x differs from an element of R by an element of c subset R, so x itself lies in R. This is the conductor fibre product in n1, not an arbitrary base-change contraction assertion. On the infinite-conductor stratum the inclusion for Q gives
  v(I_N)/(kN) <= (1+h'/N)(v(K)/k+L/k).
Everything in this estimate is evaluated on quotient primary ideals and is finite. On the finite-conductor stratum the unique lift w satisfies
  w(J)/k <= v(I_N)/(kN) <= w(J)/k+v(c)/(kN),
because cJ^N subset I_N. This second estimate is only used where v(c)<infinity; there is no infinity/N assertion and no claim of a uniform conductor bound.

The lower bound everywhere is v(I_N)/(kN)>=-h-epsilon. The finite-stratum limiting upper bound is -h+epsilon, and the quotient estimate gives at most -h+4epsilon at infinity. Since I_N^2 subset I_{2N}, b_l=v(I_{2^l})/(k2^l) is decreasing. The increasing open sets {b_l+h<5epsilon} cover the compact boundary, so one covers it. Thus -b_l in Q_R is uniformly within 5epsilon of h. Negative profiles here increase only INSIDE this approximation argument; this is not an extra increasing-limit closure operation for D. Letting epsilon go to zero proves h in C_R.

For ANY finite injection R -> B with B reduced, put B'=(B tensor_R S)_red. The map S -> B' is injective: integral Spec(B)->Spec(R) is surjective, base change is still surjective, and its kernel lies in every prime of the reduced S. The primary boundary ideal remains proper at every nonempty local-centre factor, and n1 supplies actual full fibres for all restriction maps. Pull the compatible C_B function to B'; normal-target descent centrewise produces its continuous function on S, which is h composed with S -> R by surjectivity. The normalization step then produces h in C_R. Conversely extension of primary ideals preserves C, and full-fibre surjectivity makes this pullback isometric. Vertical components and empty field factors have not been discarded from compatibility testing.

The raw normalization-compatible family N_R is consequently between Q_R and C_R: Q_R subset N_R subset C_R and the two raw families have the same uniform closure. There is no assertion Q_R=N_R or raw equality with C_R. This proof uses only the earlier LOCAL support chain and the exact integral-dependence sources checked in n2. The coverage and source records are whole-proof-coverage.md and whole-source-application-ledger.md.

notes.summary: Strictly negative D-descent passes for unbounded and partial-bottom profiles using an actual decreasing net of majorants.
notes.detailedSummary: Finite positive gaps and compact strict insertion replace unsupported nested-net flattening. Rational quotient approximation, primary-factor contraction and positive scaling construct strict C-majorants. Bottom is handled without infinity-infinity or an increasing-limit closure axiom.
notes.text:
Independent review of ACTUAL FINAL n5: mathematics PASS; essential sources PASS.

Use LOCAL n1--n4. Here D means actual decreasing C-NETS, with no increasing-limit closure. I prove descent for a fibre-constant u in D_S whose quotient h is strictly negative everywhere, allowing unbounded negative values and partial bottom. Upper semicontinuity follows from the quotient map. Compactness gives h<=-c for SOME FINITE c>0; if all values are bottom, the sequence -Nv(a) already supplies descent. Normal targets use n3. For a normalization step, restrict to the conductor quotient and apply dimension induction to obtain h0 in D_(R/c)_red.

The key is strict insertion, not flattening nested nets. Given a finite continuous F>h, the lower semicontinuous positive function F-h has a positive compact lower bound; if its infimum is infinity choose a finite positive e nonetheless. There is never an infinity-infinity subtraction. A compact strict open-cover argument in the actual decreasing representation u=inf g_i chooses a SINGLE C_S term g with g<-c/2 and g<F composed with restriction-e/2. Directedness selects one index for the finitely many covering inequalities. Choose a small b>0 with b||g||<e/8. Scaling to (1-b)g creates a positive uniform gap above finite u (at least bc/2); a rational primary-profile approximation j=-w(J)/k then satisfies u+s<=j<F composed with restriction-e/8 for some s>0. Bottom points automatically satisfy the lower inequality. Let M=||j||.

For quotient insertion choose b1>0 so b1 M<s/4. Since u<=j-s, for finite values (1-b1)u<=j+b1 M-(1-b1)s<j-s/4 after reducing b1; at bottom the same inequality is immediate. A compact selection from a decreasing representation of h0 produces a scaled term below j on the quotient and strictly negative, and sufficiently accurate rational approximation gives kappa=-v(K)/k>=h0 and kappa pulled to E<j_E+delta. The lower inequality follows because scaling a strictly negative majorant of h0 creates a uniform positive gap before rational approximation. Synchronize denominators so 1/k<delta. Choose k delta<L<=k delta+1 with L>0. Q=KE(aE)^L is integral over JE on ALL components, including the empty-boundary zero-dimensional ones, and n2 supplies a common h'.

The exact contraction argument of n4 yields an INTERNAL increasing dyadic family f_l=-v(I_{2^l})/(k2^l), with f_l<=j and limiting lower bound >=kappa-2delta>=h-2delta at infinite conductor. At finite conductor the limit is j>=h+s. The open sets {f_l>h-3delta} cover the compact boundary, including bottom points, because f_l-h is lower semicontinuous. Select one finite profile f. Put eta=3delta/c and choose delta sufficiently small that eta<1/2 and eta M<e/16. Then q=(1-eta)f belongs to C_R. For finite h<=-c,
  q>(1-eta)(h-3delta)=h+eta(-h)-3delta+3delta eta>=h+3delta eta;
for bottom, a finite q is strictly above h. Also f<=j<=0 implies q<=j+eta M<F. Hence h<q<F. This uses positive scaling, not subtraction in D.

All strict C_R-majorants of h are downward directed: insert below the minimum of two of them. Order this set by reverse pointwise order to obtain an ACTUAL decreasing C_R-net. Its infimum is h. To verify the last statement, if t>h(v), upper semicontinuity and compact Hausdorff separation provide a finite continuous F>h with F(v)<t; insertion produces a C-majorant below it. This works at h(v)=-infinity as well, for any finite t. It completes the dimension induction without assuming increasing closure, interchanging unsupported iterated nets, or writing infinity-infinity.

The same normalization/reduced-base-change construction as n4 treats every reduced finite injection, via full fibres and the normal-target traces of n3. Field factors have empty boundaries; vertical positive-dimensional factors participate in fibre constancy but receive no invented generic degree. Actual n5 therefore passes for strictly negative, all-bottom and partial-bottom profiles. Mixed zero is addressed separately by n6, not silently replaced by strict negativity. Details of this proof are retained in whole-proof.md.

notes.summary: Mixed-zero D-descent passes using divisorial density, the normal-centre zero dichotomy and positive descent of an active indicator.
notes.detailedSummary: Support-safe ratio charts and exact Rees/dimension formulas establish characteristic-free divisorial density. The indicator descends through C with positivity. Strict majorants preserve true zero off a clopen active set and partial bottom on it; full finite-source fibres survive normalization/base change.
notes.text:
Independent review of ACTUAL FINAL n6: mathematics PASS; essential sources PASS.

Use LOCAL n1--n5. The missing step for mixed zero is an independently proved zero dichotomy on each normal local centre. First prove divisorial density on an excellent local DOMAIN without an SNC assumption. For a given supportful normalized v, choose a primary generator a0 with v(a0)=1. In a finite-coordinate basic neighbourhood, adjoin all a_j/a0 to a finite-type birational chart B0. For each finite positive coordinate value v(f), choose rational bounds p/q<v(f)<r/s and adjoin f^q/a0^p and a0^r/f^s. For an infinite value impose only a lower bound. Every denominator has finite value, so evaluation takes place through the support quotient and its valued fraction field. Its positive prime P contains a0 and the strict-ratio elements, and contracts to m. Choose an m_(B0_P)-Rees DVR nu of this excellent positive-dimensional local domain. Its restrictions satisfy the same strict inequalities and nu(a)=nu(a0)>0, so after normalization it lies in the prescribed neighbourhood. By the exact dimension formula and Rees residue formula proved with their hypotheses in n2,
  trdeg_k kappa(nu)=trdeg_k kappa(P)+dim(B0_P)-1=dim R-1.
It is discrete rank one and therefore divisorial in the sense required by Rond--Spivakovsky. Units and zero coordinates impose their forced values. This proves density for all valuation supports in arbitrary characteristic.

Now let R be NORMAL. For a fixed divisorial nu, n2 gives nu(f)<=C_nu ord_m(f) for nonunits, with units handled separately. On an a-section, v0(m)>=1/r, hence ord_m(f)<=r v0(f). Choosing an ideal generator of least finite v0-value gives nu(I)<=C_nu r v0(I). For negative finite REAL sums of ideal profiles this says g(nu)>=C_nu r g(v0); it passes to uniform limits. If g in C_R has g(v0)=0, nonpositivity forces g(nu)=0 for every divisorial nu; density and continuity force g=0. If h in D_R vanishes at v0, EVERY term of its decreasing C-net vanishes there, since it lies between h and zero; each term is identically zero. Thus on a normal centre a D-function is either identically zero or strictly negative at every point, possibly bottom at some points. Compactness bounds each nonzero component above by a finite negative constant.

For normalization S, mark the finitely many active local-centre pieces where the fibre-constant u is nonzero. An active piece and an inactive one cannot meet the same fibre: one gives a strictly negative value and the other zero. The indicator sigma=-1 on active pieces, 0 on inactive pieces belongs to C_S by Chinese-remainder gluing of primary/unit profiles. Its continuous, fibre-constant descent is in C_R BY THE POSITIVE DESCENT THEOREM n4, not merely by quotient topology. Let T={sigma=-1}; it is clopen. The quotient h is zero outside T and h<=-c on T for some finite c>0. Empty T gives zero; if all active values are bottom, the decreasing sequence N sigma gives the required exact zero complement and bottom on T.

For the general active part, adding a negative constant to u puts it in the strictly negative case, so n5 supplies h-delta in D_R for every delta>0. This does NOT justify an increasing limit as delta decreases to zero. Instead fix a finite continuous F>h on T and a finite positive compact gap e. Choose eta small with eta(||F||+e)<e/4 and delta=eta c/[2(1-eta)]. On finite active values,
  (1-eta)(h-delta)=h+eta(-h-c/2)>h,
and this scaled target is below F-e/2; at bottom it stays bottom. A compact selection from the actual decreasing C-net for h-delta gives a term g with (1-eta)g<F-e/4 on T. Choose N>0 with -N<min_T F and set q=max((1-eta)g,N sigma). This is in C_R; it has h<q<F on T and is EXACTLY zero off T, because every C-function is nonpositive. The positive gap persists at finite h, and partial-bottom points cause no arithmetic ambiguity.

These strict majorants with zero complement are downward directed by inserting below the minimum of two. Continuous separation on the compact clopen T proves their infimum is h, as in n5. They furnish one ACTUAL decreasing C_R-net and establish mixed-zero D-descent. Combining normalization with the injective reduced base change and full fibres in n4 gives the same statement for ANY reduced finite injection, including vertical components and empty zero-dimensional factors. Pullback identifies C and D with their actual fibre-constant subclasses. Gauge covariance follows n1. The proof neither imposes a target-domain shortcut on general maps nor introduces increasing-limit or subtraction closure.

The essential source inputs are exactly the excellent-domain dimension/Rees statements and the normal-domain analytic Izumi bound reconstructed in n2. No singular or positive-characteristic resolution theorem is used. The resulting general conductor rule is geometric as well once n8 proves comparison.

Their radical contains t^2,t^3 and then z, so they are proper primary. Write s=w(t), u=w(z), B=w(b). Every generator has value at least kA.
